name: Question 10
problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets ${x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-{z}^{2}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-{z}^{2} & =-1 \\ {x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1 & ={z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1 \\ z & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
{x}^{2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$

Question 10
?

Given the hyperboloid of two sheets x2+(y−3)29−z2=−1, find the domain of z=z(x,y).

a
{(x,y):x2+(y−3)29>1}
b
{(x,y):x2+(y−3)29≤1}
c
{(x,y):x2+(y−3)29≥1}
d
R2
e
{(x,y):x2+(y−3)29<1}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the hyperboloid equation, we make z the subject as follows: x2+(y−3)29−z2=−1x2+(y−3)29+1=z2

z2=x2+(y−3)29+1z=±x2+(y−3)29+1

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all (x,y)∈R2, we have x2+(y−3)29+1≥0.

Therefore, the domain of z(x,y) is R2.
